REPORT ON Esperanto School and alleged plans to make it
centre of Bolshevist activities.
Made by D. S. I. Givens Forwarded by Chief Detective Officer.

Sir,

A Russian named Vadim A. Stodany 71 Broadway
Terrace, who is a book-keeper in the Russian Publishing
and Printing Co., No. 35 Broadway Road, and a Chinese
named Loh Sih Kya( 陸式楷), who works in the Australian
Products Co., No. 67A Ward Road, have started a free
school for teaching Esperanto at No. Y1640 N. Szechuen
Road, where some thirty pupils attend on Monday,
Wednesday and Friday evenings.

Inter. Koo of the C. I. D. Headquarters, whose
connection with the S. M. P. is not generally known,
has interviewed Loh. The latter told Koo that he and
his Russian colleague were working in the interests of
Bolshevism, and added that G. Kun alias Zung Bai Koong
( 鄭佩剛) is in charge of the headquarters of their
society which are in Canton. As soon as the pupils
in the N. Szechuen Road School are able to read Esperanto
books in that language explaining the tenets of Bolshevism
will be supplied to them from the Canton headquarters.

Inter. Koo will attend the Esperanto classes
and watch developments.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
J.H.Givens
D. S. I.

关于世界语学校及涉嫌将其作为布尔什维克活动中心的计划的报告。
由副督察吉文斯（D. S. I. Givens）撰写，经首席探员转呈。

先生：

一名名为瓦迪姆·A·斯托达尼（Vadim A. Stodany）的俄国人，住址为百老汇路71号 terrace，系百老汇路35号俄国出版印刷公司（Russian Publishing and Printing Co.）的簿记员；以及一名名为陆式楷（Loh Sih Kya）的华人，系华德路67A号澳洲产品公司（Australian Products Co.）职员，两人在北四川路Y1640号开办了一所免费的世界语学校，每周一、三、五晚间约有三十名学生上课。

刑事侦缉处总部的翻译员顾（Koo），其与工部局警务处的关系并不为外人所知，已约谈了陆式楷。后者告诉顾，他和他的俄国同事正为布尔什维主义的利益工作，并补充说，郑佩刚（G. Kun，别名 Zung Bai Koong）负责该社团位于广州的总部。一旦北四川路学校的学生能够阅读世界语书籍，解释布尔什维主义信条的书籍将从广州总部提供给他们。

翻译员顾将出席世界语课程并监视事态发展。

此致，
您顺从的仆人，
J.H.吉文斯

Certain persons used to satirize anarchists :-
"The anarchists idea is good but their name is not,
because anarchy means disorder and disturbance. Alas !
Why do they want to teach people this as it endangers
the peace".

Do these satirists mistake the name of our party
for that which will oppose good order and favour dis-
turbance ? We are willing to argue with them as to
what they mean by good order. Is good order as they
understand it the same as what we believe ? To us,
good order means abolition of class, distinction, taking
the people of the world as one family or one person, each
to work for the public good. Is good order as they
understand it the same as this ? We don't think so.
No matter what the real state of the future may be, and
judging by the present condition of bad order, those who
satirize us as persons who desire the disturbing of good
order, are requested to observe how we will disturb good
order.

Communism will never die. Does it not mean "Do what you like and get what you want" ? The man who first advocated it was Louis Blane, a well known French socialist. L. Blane was born in 1813 and died in 1882. In the middle of the 19th century socialism advocated by "St. Simmen Folis" and others became unpopular in France and was tabooed in Germany. L. 共产主义永远不会消亡。它难道不意味着“各尽所能，各取所需”吗？最早倡导这一思想的是著名的法国社会主义者路易·勃朗（Louis Blane）。L. Blane 生于1813年，卒于1882年。19世纪中叶，由“圣西门傅立叶”等人倡导的社会主义在法国不再流行，并在德国被列为禁忌。L. Blane 致力于联合两国的社会主义者，他的努力推动了社会主义的发展。虽然 L. Blane 一生关注政治事务并因此不受青睐，但他的学说“各尽所能，各取所需”是我们应当了解的共产主义社会主义原则。下面我们转载其著作《劳动组织》（Organization de Travail）中最精彩的部分。

Sir,
Towards the end of April 1920 news reached Shanghai that General Chen Chin Ming, Changchowfu, Fokien, was carrying on propaganda in favour of Bolshevism. On 27th April, a communication was received from H. B. M. Consulate General to the effect that a paper published by General Chen at Changchowfu contained an advertisement urging supporters of Bolsheviks to register at Box 105, Chinese Post Office, Shanghai. The Chinese Military Authorities, whose assistance was sought in pursuing the inquiries started in consequence of the above information, had already commenced investigations and discovered that Box 105 C. P. O. was rented by a person who had given the name of Zung Pih Teh (陳必達), but had not furnished his address. The box was cleared from time to time by Zung's agent who took the letters, etc. to the Enquiry Office of the Oriental Hotel.

Dear Kaung( 剛 ),

I have duly noted your letter. The two letters I sent
to you some time ago were addressed C/O Mr. Keh S( 克水 ).
Why did they not reach you ? Sung Bah( 聲白 ) has come out,
please don't worry. With regard to the book entitled "Notes
of a Traveller (旅俄見聞記) in Russia", we will enter into direct negotia-
tions with the "Daily Morning Post"( 晨報 ). Please
write to the "Daily Morning Post" from the printing company.

deter us. The book, "The Aged Love"( 愛的成年 ), which was
translated by my friend "Hou Han"( 厚厂 ) and which advocates
free love will soon be published. Why did Keh S( 克水 )
and Shang Foong( 香風 ) return to Shanghai ? It is reported

a case known ? How are Ping Yuan( 冰絲 ) and Zah Sing( 石心 )
getting on ? Why don't Keh( 克 ) tell me about them ?
Please give me full details. I did not receive the May Day
hardbills distributed in Shanghai which you said you had
mailed to me. I think they have been stolen. Be careful
when sending letters. It is best for you to mail all communi-
cations at the French Office( ? 法國局 ).

REPORT ON Developments in Inquiry re Holder of Box 105 C. P. O.
at which Chinese Bolsheviks are requested to register.

Made by D. I. Givens Forwarded by Chief Detective Officer.

Sir,

With reference to attached, C. D. C.s 101 Zia Vee Tsong
(謝維中) and 98 Bah Tsoong Ji (白鐘麒) were placed on
20th instant to watch the Inquiry Office of the Oriental Hotel,
arrangements having been previously made with an informer on
the staff of that establishment to let them know when letters
were brought there addressed to Box No. 105, Chinese Post Office.
About 9.15 a.m. 21st instant, the informer told C. D. C. 101
that such a letter had arrived, and added that an employe of
the Inquiry Office named Tsang Ts Ying (張子英) had put it
into his pocket. Tsang left the hotel XXXXXX about an hour
later and the detectives followed him. He first proceeded to
Wah Cheng (華強書局) printing establishment, No. 140 Rue Hue,
French Town and later went to No. 4 Li Ts Li (聯珠里),
Avenue Edward VII (French Concession).

Tsang again visited the Wah Cheng (華強書局) printing
establishment at 7.30 p.m. on May 21st.

The detectives are remaining on watch at the Oriental
Hotel, and enquiries are being made about the address where
Tsang called.

Further
OM

Your obedient servant,
D.I.Givens
